newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: U.S., Centam to sign "open-skies" airline accord.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Centam to sign "open-skies" airline accord.

text.p: The United States and Central American nations will sign on Thursday an "open-skies" airline accord, the Costa Rican Foreign Minister Fernando Naranjo said Wednesday.
The accord, marking the visit of U.S. President Bill Clinton, will allow airlines of signing nations freedom of routes across the region.
"The undestanding behind the accord is to foster an international system of transport based on the concept of open competition in the airline market," Naranjo said in a statement.
Signing nations from Central American will be Costa Rica, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala.

Naranjo said airlines from both regions would be able to offer a wider range of services after the accord, with lower passenger tariffs. Naranjo said Central American airlines would likely increase the number of flights to the United States.
"This new situation will also help boost exports from Central America...as well to promote investments and bring a greater flow of U.S. tourists to the Central American region," he added.

Clinton arrives late Wednesday here in the Costa Rican capital for a visit scheduled that ends at midday on Friday. He will meet the heads of state of Guatemala, Belize, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and the Dominican Republic.
